Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty.         """Project each steady deep forecast regression-wave cadence past the last wave.

        Reuses every public input, parameter order, validation order,
        stage cap, wave construction, recurrence aggregation,
        periodicity filtering and sorting, over-limit error and
        frozen-view semantic of
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_backtests_scorecards_regression_wave_periodicities`,
        appending
        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon`` and
        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit``
        in that order after
        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_periodicity_limit``
        (still before the split membership check and any state lookup),
        keeping the same optional trailing ``token``. Both must be
        non-``bool`` :class:`int` values of at least one (a ``bool`` or
        non-:class:`int` raises :class:`TypeError`, a non-positive value
        raises :class:`ValueError`).

        Every stage runs exactly once, exactly as in the deep regression
        wave periodicity query: the one frozen view produces exactly the
        complete periodicity record set a deep regression wave
        periodicities call with the same arguments would return, with
        every underlying stage cap and every underlying exception
        unchanged. The serial number of the last wave of the complete
        deep regression wave set in that view is the observation
        boundary. For each periodicity record, candidate waves start at
        the record's own ``last_wave`` and advance by its median
        ``period`` one ordinal at a time; a candidate is kept only when
        strictly greater than the boundary and at most the boundary plus
        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon``, so
        the range is never truncated and no prediction is ever
        represented as an observed wave.

        The result is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
        ``forecasts, totals``. Each kept record is a fresh dict
        reproducing every periodicity field in the same order --
        ``identity, waves, first_wave, last_wave, span, points,
        peak_active, appearances, intervals, period, jitter`` -- and
        appending a ``forecasts`` tuple in ascending ordinal order;
        each prediction is a fresh dict with keys ordered ``ordinal,
        wave, earliest, latest``, where ``ordinal`` is the one-based
        order after the identity's last appearance, ``wave`` is
        ``last_wave + ordinal * period`` and ``earliest``/``latest`` are
        ``last_wave + ordinal * min(intervals)`` and
        ``last_wave + ordinal * max(intervals)``. A record with no
        candidate in range is dropped; the kept records preserve the
        periodicity sort order. ``totals`` is a fresh dict with keys
        ordered ``identities, predictions, waves, points, first_wave,
        last_wave``: the kept-identity count, the summed prediction
        count, the summed participating-wave count, the summed point
        count and the earliest and latest participating wave numbers
        (six zeros when the record set is empty).
        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit``
        bounds the complete candidate set measured across every
        prediction, not every identity, so an over-limit query raises
        :class:`ValueError` without truncating or returning partial
        records. Every object is built fresh and shares nothing with
        the periodicity records or internal state; a tokenized success
        consumes exactly one read while any failure refunds it, and a
        tokenless query observes the same frozen view and never mutates
        branches, the event graph, snapshot quotas or persistence files.
        """

        # order, but no branch or historical node is looked up yet.
        validated = self._validate_frontier_inputs(

def _build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_backtests_result(
        wave_records: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        regression_wave_min_regression_wave_occurrences: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_recurrence_limit: int,
        regression_wave_max_regression_wave_jitter: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_periodicity_limit: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_cutoffs: tuple[int, ...],
        regression_wave_regression_wave_match_tolerance: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_backtest_limit: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Score each cutoff's prefix-trained projections on later waves.

        Used only by
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_backtests`.
        The wave records are the complete, already-bounded ``waves``
        tuple of
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_waves_result`,
        so each wave's position in the tuple is its zero-based serial
        number and the last serial is the observation end. When the
        wave set is non-empty, every cutoff beyond its last serial
        raises :class:`ValueError` before any training runs; an empty
        wave set skips the range check and scores nothing.

        Each cutoff reruns the recurrence and periodicity aggregations
        on the prefix of waves with serial numbers at most the cutoff,
        with ``regression_wave_min_regression_wave_occurrences``,
        ``regression_wave_max_regression_wave_jitter`` and the two
        stage caps applied exactly as in the forecasts query, and then
        projects each kept identity's cadence from its last training
        wave by its median period, keeping only predicted waves
        strictly greater than the cutoff and at most
        ``cutoff + regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon``.
        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit`` bounds each
        cutoff's complete prediction set exactly as in the forecasts
        query. The evaluation window is the observed serials greater
        than the cutoff and at most
        ``cutoff + regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon``; targets
        claim same-identity appearances in that window in ascending
        target order, nearest first, equal distances going to the
        earlier wave, never reusing an appearance. A claimed target is
        ``hit``; an unclaimed one is ``missed`` when its wave does not
        exceed the observation end and ``unresolved`` when it does;
        unclaimed window appearances count as ``unexpected``.

        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_backtest_limit``
        bounds the complete cross-cutoff record set, enforced only
        once the set is built, so an over-limit query raises
        :class:`ValueError` without truncating. Records sort by cutoff
        ascending and then keep the cutoff's periodicity order;
        ``totals`` counts the represented cutoffs, the records and the
        four outcome counters. Every record, appearance, target and
        totals dict is built fresh and shares no mutable object with
        the wave records.
        """
        last_wave = len(wave_records) - 1
        if wave_records:
            # A cutoff's range is only meaningful once the wave set
            # exists; an empty wave set scores nothing at all.
            for cutoff in regression_wave_regression_wave_cutoffs:
                if cutoff > last_wave:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"forecast regression wave cutoff {cutoff} is "
                        f"out of range for {last_wave + 1} forecast "
                        f"regression wave(s)"
                    )

        # Each identity's observed wave serials, ascending, answer
        # every cutoff's matching from the one observation set.
        serials_by_identity: dict[object, list[int]] = {}
        for serial, wave in enumerate(wave_records):
            present: set[object] = set()
            for point in wave["points"]:
                for identity in point["identities"]:
                    present.add(identity)
            for identity in present:
                serials_by_identity.setdefault(identity, []).append(serial)

        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for cutoff in regression_wave_regression_wave_cutoffs:
            # Training sees only waves with serial numbers at most the
            # cutoff; the recurrence, periodicity and forecast stages
            # rerun on that prefix with their own caps, so every
            # record's cadence, order and projections come from the
            # prefix alone.
            recurrences = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_recurrences_result(
                wave_records[: cutoff + 1],
                regression_wave_min_regression_wave_occurrences,
                regression_wave_regression_wave_recurrence_limit,
            )
            periodicities = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_periodicities_result(
                recurrences["recurrences"],
                regression_wave_max_regression_wave_jitter,
                regression_wave_regression_wave_periodicity_limit,
            )
            forecasts = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_forecasts_result(
                periodicities["periodicities"],
                cutoff,
                regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon,
                regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit,
            )
            window_end = cutoff + regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon
            for forecast in forecasts["forecasts"]:
                identity = forecast["identity"]

                # cutoff and inside the evaluation window, ascending.
                reals = [
                    serial
                    for serial in serials_by_identity.get(identity, ())
                    if cutoff < serial <= window_end

                used = [False] * len(reals)
                targets: list[dict[str, object]] = []
                hit = 0
                missed = 0
                unresolved = 0
                for prediction in forecast["forecasts"]:
                    target_wave = prediction["wave"]
                    best_index: int | None = None

        order, and the four outcome counters sum over every one of the
        identity's records.

        ``identity, cutoffs, hit, missed, unresolved, unexpected,

        ``hit_rate`` is the reduced ``(hit, evaluated)`` integer

            entry["missed"] += record["missed"]
            entry["unresolved"] += record["unresolved"]

                    entry["missed"],

            # real fractions are compared by cross-multiplication.

                left[identity_index]
            )
            right_key = BranchStore._lifetime_identity_unicode_key(
                right[identity_index]
            )
            if left_key < right_key:
                return -1
            if left_key > right_key:

                f"regression wave forecast scorecard regression wave "

                f"{regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_limit}"

        identities_total = 0

        missed_total = 0
        unresolved_total = 0
        unexpected_total = 0
        evaluated_total = 0
        for entry in kept_entries:

            identities_total += 1
            hit_total += entry["hit"]
            missed_total += entry["missed"]
            unresolved_total += entry["unresolved"]
            unexpected_total += entry["unexpected"]

            missed_total,
            unresolved_total,
            unexpected_total,
            evaluated_total,

def _build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_backtests_scorecards_regression_wave_forecasts_result(
        periodicity_records: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        boundary: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Project each steady deep forecast regression-wave cadence forward.

        Used only by
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_backtests_scorecards_regression_wave_forecasts`.
        The records are the complete, already-bounded and
        already-sorted ``periodicities`` tuple of
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_backtests_scorecards_regression_wave_periodicities_result`,
        and ``boundary`` is the serial number of the last deep
        regression wave in the wave set (``-1`` when no deep
        regression wave qualified). For each record, candidate waves
        start at the record's own ``last_wave`` and advance by its
        median ``period`` one ordinal at a time; a candidate is kept
        only when strictly greater than ``boundary`` and at most
        ``boundary + regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon``,
        so the range is never truncated. Each prediction is a fresh
        ``ordinal, wave, earliest, latest`` dict: ``ordinal`` is the
        one-based order after the identity's last appearance, ``wave``
        is ``last_wave + ordinal * period`` and
        ``earliest``/``latest`` are
        ``last_wave + ordinal * min(intervals)`` and
        ``last_wave + ordinal * max(intervals)``.

        A record with no candidate in range is dropped; every kept
        record is a fresh copy of the periodicity record with every
        field in the same order and an appended ascending-ordinal
        ``forecasts`` tuple, keeping the periodicity sort order. The
        complete prediction set is built before the
        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit``
        cap -- measured across every prediction, not every identity --
        is enforced, so an over-limit query raises :class:`ValueError`
        without returning partial records. ``totals`` is a fresh dict
        ordered ``identities, predictions, waves, points, first_wave,
        last_wave`` holding the kept-identity count, the summed
        prediction count, the summed participating-wave count, the
        summed point count and the earliest and latest participating
        wave numbers (six zeros when nothing projects); no prediction
        is ever represented as an observed wave. Every record,
        appearance and prediction dict is built fresh and shares no
        mutable object with the periodicity records.
        """
        upper = boundary + regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon
        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        prediction_count = 0
        total_waves = 0
        total_points = 0
        for record in periodicity_records:
            last_wave = record["last_wave"]
            period = record["period"]
            intervals = record["intervals"]
            smallest = min(intervals)
            largest = max(intervals)

            forecasts: list[dict[str, object]] = []
            ordinal = 1
            while True:
                wave = last_wave + ordinal * period
                if wave > upper:
                    break
                if wave > boundary:
                    forecasts.append(
                        {
                            "ordinal": ordinal,
                            "wave": wave,
                            "earliest": last_wave + ordinal * smallest,
                            "latest": last_wave + ordinal * largest,
                        }
                    )
                ordinal += 1
            if not forecasts:
                continue

            records.append(
                {
                    "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(
                        record["identity"]
                    ),
                    "waves": record["waves"],
                    "first_wave": record["first_wave"],
                    "last_wave": last_wave,
                    "span": record["span"],
                    "points": record["points"],
                    "peak_active": record["peak_active"],
                    "appearances": tuple(
                        dict(appearance)
                        for appearance in record["appearances"]
                    ),
                    "intervals": tuple(
                        interval for interval in intervals
                    ),
                    "period": period,
                    "jitter": record["jitter"],
                    "forecasts": tuple(forecasts),
                }
            )
            prediction_count += len(forecasts)
            total_waves += record["waves"]
            total_points += record["points"]

        if prediction_count > regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn drift wave prediction scorecard "
                f"regression wave forecast scorecard regression wave "
                f"forecast backtest scorecard regression wave "
                f"forecast limit exceeded: {prediction_count} prediction "
                f"records, limit is "
                f"{regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit}"
            )

        totals = {
            "identities": len(records),
            "predictions": prediction_count,
            "waves": total_waves,
            "points": total_points,
            "first_wave": 0,
            "last_wave": 0,
        }
        if records:
            totals["first_wave"] = min(
                record["first_wave"] for record in records
            )
            totals["last_wave"] = max(
                record["last_wave"] for record in records
            )
        return {"forecasts": tuple(records), "totals": totals}

        then projects each kept identity's waves from its last
        training wave by its median period, keeping only offsets of at
        most ``wave_horizon``. The evaluation window is the observed
        serials greater than the cutoff and at most ``cutoff +
        wave_horizon``; targets claim same-identity appearances in
        that window in ascending target order, nearest first, equal
        distances going to the earlier wave, never reusing an
        appearance. A claimed target is ``hit``; an unclaimed one is
        ``missed`` when it does not exceed the observation end and
        ``unresolved`` when it does; unclaimed window appearances
        count as ``unexpected``.

        ``prediction_result_limit`` bounds each cutoff's complete
        record set and ``prediction_backtest_limit`` the complete
        cross-cutoff set, both enforced only once the set is built, so
        an over-limit query raises :class:`ValueError` without
        truncating. Records sort by cutoff ascending and then keep the
        cutoff's periodicity order; ``totals`` counts the represented

        record, target and totals dict is built fresh and shares no
        mutable object with the wave records.

                recurrences["recurrences"],
                max_wave_jitter,
                periodicity_result_limit,
            )

builder = f'''    @staticmethod
    def {NEW_BUILDER}(
        wave_records: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        regression_wave_regression_wave_min_regression_wave_occurrences: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_recurrence_limit: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_max_regression_wave_jitter: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_periodicity_limit: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_cutoffs: tuple[int, ...],
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_match_tolerance: int,
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_backtest_limit: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Score each cutoff's prefix-trained projections on later waves.

        :meth:`{NEW_NAME}`.
        The wave records are the complete, already-bounded ``waves``
        tuple of
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_scorecard_regression_wave_forecast_backtests_scorecards_regression_waves_result`,

        number and the last serial is the observation end. When the
        wave set is non-empty, every cutoff beyond its last serial
        raises :class:`ValueError` before any training runs; an empty
        wave set skips the range check and scores nothing.

        Each cutoff reruns the recurrence and periodicity aggregations
        on the prefix of waves with serial numbers at most the cutoff,
        with
        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_min_regression_wave_occurrences``,
        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_max_regression_wave_jitter``
        and the two stage caps applied exactly as in the forecasts
        query, and then projects each kept identity's cadence from its
        last training wave by its median period, keeping only
        predicted waves strictly greater than the cutoff and at most
        ``cutoff +
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon``.

        bounds each cutoff's complete prediction set exactly as in the
        forecasts query. The evaluation window is the observed serials
        greater than the cutoff and at most ``cutoff +
        regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon``;
        targets claim same-identity appearances in that window in
        ascending target order, nearest first, equal distances going
        to the earlier wave, never reusing an appearance. A claimed
        target is ``hit``; an unclaimed one is ``missed`` when its
        wave does not exceed the observation end and ``unresolved``
        when it does; unclaimed window appearances count as
        ``unexpected``.

        ``regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_backtest_limit``
        bounds the complete cross-cutoff record set, enforced only
        once the set is built, so an over-limit query raises
        :class:`ValueError` without truncating. Records sort by cutoff
        ascending and then keep the cutoff's periodicity order;
        ``totals`` counts the represented cutoffs, the records and the
        four outcome counters. Every record, appearance, target and
        totals dict is built fresh and shares no mutable object with
        the wave records.

            # exists; an empty wave set scores nothing at all.
            for cutoff in regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_cutoffs:

                    raise ValueError(
                        f"deep regression wave cutoff {{cutoff}} is out "
                        f"of range for {{last_wave + 1}} deep regression "
                        f"wave(s)"

        # Each identity's observed wave serials, ascending, answer
        # every cutoff's matching from the one observation set.
        serials_by_identity: dict[object, list[int]] = {{}}
        for serial, wave in enumerate(wave_records):
            present: set[object] = set()
            for point in wave["points"]:
                for identity in point["identities"]:
                    present.add(identity)
            for identity in present:
                serials_by_identity.setdefault(identity, []).append(serial)

        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for cutoff in regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_cutoffs:
            # Training sees only waves with serial numbers at most the
            # cutoff; the recurrence, periodicity and forecast stages
            # rerun on that prefix with their own caps, so every
            # record's cadence, order and projections come from the
            # prefix alone.
            recurrences = BranchStore.{DEEP_RECURRENCES}(
                wave_records[: cutoff + 1],
                regression_wave_regression_wave_min_regression_wave_occurrences,
                regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_recurrence_limit,
            )
            periodicities = BranchStore.{DEEP_PERIODICITIES}(
                recurrences["recurrences"],
                regression_wave_regression_wave_max_regression_wave_jitter,
                regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_periodicity_limit,
            )
            forecasts = BranchStore.{DEEP_FORECASTS}(
                periodicities["periodicities"],
                cutoff,
                regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon,
                regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_limit,

            window_end = (
                cutoff
                + regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_horizon
            )
            for forecast in forecasts["forecasts"]:
                identity = forecast["identity"]
                # Observed appearances of the identity after the
                # cutoff and inside the evaluation window, ascending.
                reals = [
                    serial
                    for serial in serials_by_identity.get(identity, ())
                    if cutoff < serial <= window_end
                ]
                used = [False] * len(reals)
                targets: list[dict[str, object]] = []
                hit = 0
                missed = 0
                unresolved = 0
                for prediction in forecast["forecasts"]:
                    target_wave = prediction["wave"]
                    best_index: int | None = None
                    best_distance: int | None = None
                    for index, real in enumerate(reals):
                        if used[index]:
                            continue
                        distance = real - target_wave
                        if distance < 0:
                            distance = -distance
                        if (
                            distance
                            > regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_match_tolerance
                        ):
                            continue

                        # test keeps the earlier wave on ties.
                        if best_distance is None or distance < best_distance:
                            best_distance = distance
                            best_index = index
                    if best_index is not None:
                        used[best_index] = True
                        actual: int | None = reals[best_index]
                        status = "hit"
                        hit += 1
                    else:
                        actual = None
                        if target_wave <= last_wave:
                            status = "missed"
                            missed += 1
                        else:
                            status = "unresolved"
                            unresolved += 1
                    targets.append(
                        {{
                            "ordinal": prediction["ordinal"],
                            "wave": target_wave,
                            "earliest": prediction["earliest"],
                            "latest": prediction["latest"],
                            "actual": actual,
                            "status": status,
                        }}
                    )
                records.append(
                    {{
                        "cutoff": cutoff,
                        "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(
                            identity
                        ),
                        "waves": forecast["waves"],
                        "first_wave": forecast["first_wave"],
                        "last_wave": forecast["last_wave"],
                        "span": forecast["span"],
                        "points": forecast["points"],
                        "peak_active": forecast["peak_active"],
                        "appearances": tuple(
                            dict(appearance)
                            for appearance in forecast["appearances"]
                        ),
                        "intervals": tuple(
                            interval for interval in forecast["intervals"]
                        ),
                        "period": forecast["period"],
                        "jitter": forecast["jitter"],
                        "targets": tuple(targets),
                        "hit": hit,
                        "missed": missed,
                        "unresolved": unresolved,
                        "unexpected": used.count(False),
                    }}
                )

        if (
            len(records)
            > regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_backtest_limit
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn drift wave prediction scorecard "
                f"regression wave forecast scorecard regression wave "
                f"forecast backtest scorecard regression wave forecast "
                f"backtest limit exceeded: {{len(records)}} prediction "
                f"records across "
                f"{{len(regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_cutoffs)}} "
                f"cutoff(s), limit is "
                f"{{regression_wave_regression_wave_regression_wave_forecast_backtest_limit}}"
            )

        cutoff_seen: set[object] = set()
        totals = {{
            "cutoffs": 0,
            "records": 0,
            "hit": 0,
            "missed": 0,
            "unresolved": 0,
            "unexpected": 0,
        }}
        for record in records:
            cutoff_seen.add(record["cutoff"])

def test_training_matching_and_totals(self):
        result = build_backtests(
            synthetic_waves(), 1, 50, 0, 50, 2, 50, (4,), 0, 50
        )
        records = result["backtests"]
        # Periodicity order is A, C, B: equal jitter, then wave and
        # point counts descending, then first-encounter order.
        self.assertEqual([r["identity"] for r in records], ["A", "C", "B"])
        for record in records:
            self.assertEqual(record["cutoff"], 4)
            self.assertEqual(record["jitter"], 0)
            self.assertEqual(record["last_wave"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(records[0]["period"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(records[0]["intervals"], (1, 1, 1, 1))
        self.assertEqual(
            records[0]["targets"],
            (
                {"ordinal": 1, "wave": 5, "earliest": 5, "latest": 5,
                 "actual": 5, "status": "hit"},
                {"ordinal": 2, "wave": 6, "earliest": 6, "latest": 6,
                 "actual": None, "status": "missed"},
            ),
        )

            (records[0]["hit"], records[0]["missed"],

            (1, 1, 0, 0),

        self.assertEqual(
            [(t["wave"], t["actual"], t["status"]) for t in records[1]["targets"]],
            [(5, 5, "hit"), (6, None, "missed")],
        )
        # B's period is two, so its only target is wave 6; its wave-5
        # appearance inside the window stays unclaimed.
        self.assertEqual(records[2]["period"], 2)

            records[2]["targets"],
            ({"ordinal": 1, "wave": 6, "earliest": 6, "latest": 6,

        self.assertEqual(
